properties.claim: Every complete level multiplies perimeter by 4/3.
properties.conditions: Apply the Koch replacement once to every segment.
properties.derivation: Each old length L becomes 4 pieces of length L/3.

properties.claim: At fixed depth, doubling s doubles perimeter.
properties.conditions: Use the same construction and morph fraction.
properties.derivation: The factor multiplying s is unchanged, so P(d,2s)=2P(d,s).

definition.domain_notes: Depth 0–5, initial side 0.5–3 m. With n=floor(d) and f=d−n, P(d)=3s(4/3)^n[2/3+2√(1/36+f²/12)]. The separate Sierpinski inset is another finite construction, not the measured Koch boundary.
definition.proof_status: Count segments and multiply by their lengths. The fractional morph formula follows from the Pythagorean theorem; it is an explicit display convention.

grammar.pronunciation: At a complete level, perimeter is three times the starting side times four thirds to the level power.
grammar.formation_rule: Let n=floor(depth), f=depth-n. Output=3*length*(4/3)^n*(2/3+2*sqrt(1/36+f^2/12)). At integer levels this is 3*length*(4/3)^n. The fractional factor measures a peak raised to f times its final height.
grammar.precedence: Follow parentheses and function applications; products precede sums. Angle units and iteration conventions are explicit.
